issues.existing: bundle of swords held against the chest, blades crossing and hilts fanning upward
issues.observed: The blades do NOT cross. They lie parallel in a single gathered sheaf, all tilted the same way — points down to the viewer-left, grips and pommels fanning up to the viewer-right. What does lie across the bundle is a pair of gold cross-guards belonging to two of the swords; those are quillons crossing the blades, not blades crossing each other. (The hilts fanning upward is correct.)
issues.evidence: Carried bundle, roughly x=240-460 / y=280-430 in the 560x933 image. At 6x the blade faces above the hands run as a neat parallel fan with no intersections, and the blade tips emerging below the hands (x=190-330 / y=420-540) stay parallel all the way down.

uncertainObservations: The number of swords in the carried bundle is the thing I most want to report and the thing I am least sure of. At maximum enlargement I count 4 round pommels on wrapped grips, 2 gold cross-guards and roughly 5 bright blade faces. Blades and grips overlap, so a total of either five or six is possible; I refuse to pick one.
I count 4 blade tips emerging below his hands, but the lower tips merge into his tunic and at least one more may be hidden.
The two swords at the lower-left read to me as driven point-first into the ground, but they could instead be leaning against an unseen rock; the very tips are lost in the stones.
Whether his backward look is aimed at the tent, at the two planted swords, or simply downward cannot be settled; the eye direction is back and down to the viewer-left in all readings.
The device on the banner is a rampant quadruped, probably a lion, but it is too small to identify with confidence.
There is no clearly drawn cast shadow anywhere in this card, so I report no shadow direction.
